summary: Iteration 4: tested the convention code system, the 30-day trial and the paywall. Backend: new file test_access_conventions.py with 16 pytest tests, all passing. It covers trial creation on first call (reason=trial, 30 days left, same result on repeat calls), u_expired_demo -> access=false/expired, admin login 200/401, lockout (5 wrong attempts -> 429, and the correct password is also rejected during lockout, checked with a separate X-Forwarded-For), admin endpoints without a token or with a bad token -> 401, create code (custom lowercase saved as uppercase; auto-generated PREFIX-XXXXXX), duplicate -> 409, list (no _id), PATCH is_active persisted, DELETE then second DELETE -> 404, invalid payload -> 422. Redeem: case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed, invalid code -> 404, inactive code -> 404, max_uses reached -> 409, same user redeeming twice -> already_redeemed with no second use counted (current_uses=1), expires_at within 2 minutes of now+60 days for a 2-month code, redemptions list correct. /ai/handover with u_expired_demo -> 402 with detail.code=pro_required. Regression test_caregiver_api.py: 22/22 pass. Frontend (Playwright): an expired user on /, /paziente/x, /impostazioni and /nuovo is redirected to /pro with no back link. /pro shows the expired card, both plans (€49,90 / anno, €4,99 / mese), buy buttons disabled on web, the web billing note and the convention card; an invalid code shows the error toast. Redeeming a valid code in lowercase moves the status card to 'Premium tramite <coop>' with the expiry date, hides the plans, shows the back link, and home becomes reachable. A new user sees the banner 'Prova gratuita: 30 giorni rimasti' with a CTA to /pro (CTA hidden on /pro; banner hidden on /admin). Trial user regression: patient creation and adding a diary entry work. /admin: wrong password toast, login, create custom and auto codes, usage shown as 'X / Y attivazioni', duplicate toast, toggle switch (checked -> unchecked, 'Disattivato' badge), delete (confirm accepted), session kept after reload, logout.

action_items: Optional: fix the '1 mesi' plural in the AdminPage usage line
Consider the paywall weaknesses listed in code review (client-side only gating, resettable trial)
critical_code_review_comments: The paywall is enforced only by the frontend (AccessGate). The backend checks access only on /ai/handover. /patients, /entries, /trend etc. are open to expired users, so anyone calling the API directly gets the full app. Acceptable for an MVP, but be aware of it.

The trial is keyed on a client-generated app_user_id in localStorage. Clearing app data, reinstalling, or sending any new app_user_id gives a fresh 30-day trial. Consider tying it to the RevenueCat anonymous ID plus a device ID, or to Play Integrity.
/ai/handover skips gating entirely when app_user_id is omitted (the field is optional). A caller can simply leave it out to bypass the 402. Make it required, or treat a missing ID as no access.
The redeem endpoint has no rate limit, so codes can be brute-forced. Auto codes are prefix + 6 hex chars (16.7M combinations) and custom codes like TEST2026 are guessable. Add per-IP throttling.
Redeeming a different code while a convention is active overwrites the current convention, even if it is shorter, and uses up a slot. Consider blocking this or keeping the later expiry.

Admin lockout trusts the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header. An attacker can rotate the header to get unlimited password attempts. Use the rightmost or ingress-trusted IP, or also add a global counter.
The admin token is stored in sessionStorage (no httpOnly cookie). This is fine for a single-password internal admin page.
AccessGate fails open on network errors (reason=offline -> access=true). Intentional, but it also means blocking the API grants access.
App.js is still about 1480 lines; splitting it is overdue.
